questions.question: For observed values $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ with $n\ge2$ and mean $\bar x$, which expression is the sample standard deviation $s$?
Delivery times are recorded in minutes and their sample variance $s^2$ is computed. In which unit is the sample standard deviation $s=\sqrt{s^2}$ expressed?
options: No unit; it is a pure number

questions.question: Observations $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ ($n\ge2$, not all equal) have mean $\bar x$ and sample standard deviation $s$. They are converted to $z_j=(x_j-\bar x)/s$. What are the mean and the sample standard deviation of $z_1,\ldots,z_n$?
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be i.i.d. with standard deviation $\sigma>0$, with sample standard deviation $S_n$. Does $S_n$ tend to shrink towards $0$ as the sample size $n$ grows?
options: Yes: like the spread of $\bar X_n$, it falls as $\sigma/\sqrt n$
Yes: the factor $1/(n-1)$ in front of the sum drives it to $0$
No: $S_n$ is a guess for $\sigma$, and $\mathbb{E}[S_n^2]=\sigma^2$ for every $n$
No: it grows, because more squared deviations are added up

questions.question: For the observed data $3,5,7$, what is the sample standard deviation $s$?
Observations $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ ($n\ge2$) have sample standard deviation $s=4$. What is the sample standard deviation of the transformed values $y_j=10-3x_j$?
A sample consists of $n=4$ observations: the value $1$ occurs twice and the value $3$ occurs twice. What is the sample standard deviation $s$?
Lengths measured in metres have sample variance $s^2=0.04$ m$^2$. What is their sample standard deviation in centimetres?
Package weights have mean $\bar x=500$ g and sample standard deviation $s=8$ g. How many sample standard deviations above the mean is a package of $515$ g?

Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ ($n\ge2$) be i.i.d. with variance $\sigma^2$, so the sample variance satisfies $\mathbb{E}[S_n^2]=\sigma^2$. Which statement about $\mathbb{E}[S_n]$ holds for every such distribution?
options: $\mathbb{E}[S_n]=\sigma$, since the root of an unbiased guess is unbiased

questions.question: From one sample of i.i.d. observations ($n\ge2$) with unknown standard deviation $\sigma$, a student finds $s=4.1$ and concludes $\sigma\ge4.1$, because $\mathbb{E}[S_n]\le\sigma$. Is this conclusion justified?
options: Yes: an inequality between expectations holds for every outcome
No: $\mathbb{E}[S_n]\le\sigma$ concerns the average over samples; one $s$ can exceed $\sigma$
No: unbiasedness of $S_n^2$ forces $s=\sigma$, so $\sigma$ equals $4.1$
No: the $n-1$ divisor makes every $s$ at least $\sigma$, so $\sigma\le4.1$

questions.question: For $n=10$ observations, a calculator reports the divisor-$n$ standard deviation $\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}\sum_{j=1}^{10}(x_j-\bar x)^2}=3$. What is their sample standard deviation $s$?
The data $2,4,6$ have sample standard deviation $2$. If the $6$ is mistyped as $12$, what sample standard deviation is computed from $2,4,12$?
For the data $1,2,3,4,10$, how many observations lie within one sample standard deviation of the mean, that is in $[\bar x-s,\bar x+s]$?
For the data $0,0,3$, the mean is $1$ and the average distance from the mean is $\frac{1}{3}(1+1+2)=4/3$. What is the sample standard deviation $s$?

A student claims that for every data set at least half of the observations lie in the band $[\bar x-s,\bar x+s]$, where $\bar x$ is the mean and $s$ the sample standard deviation. Which assessment of this claim is correct?
options: True: $s$ is a typical distance from $\bar x$, so most points lie within it
True: about $68\%$ of any data set lies within one $s$ of $\bar x$
False, but only for tiny samples such as $n=2$ observations
False: for $-3,-3,-3,-3,0,0,3,3,3,3$ only the two zeros lie within

questions.question: Two groups, each with at least $2$ observations, have the same sample standard deviation $s_0>0$. They are combined into one data set. Which statement about the sample standard deviation $s$ of the combined data is correct?
options: It can fall below $s_0$ (equal group means) or exceed it (distant means)
It equals $s_0$, because both groups are equally spread
It is at least $s_0$, with equality when the group means coincide
It is at most $s_0$, because adding observations lowers the spread

questions.question: Five observations $x_1,\ldots,x_5$ have range $\max_j x_j-\min_j x_j=8$. What is the smallest possible value of their sample standard deviation $s$?
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_5$ be i.i.d. with variance $\sigma^2=1$, and suppose their sample standard deviation $S_5$ has $\operatorname{Var}(S_5)=0.19$. What is $\mathbb{E}[S_5]$?
